basis: Congenital dystrophy with defining seizure/neurodevelopmental manifestations; progressive hearing impairment in 1/2 assessed patients. Respiratory failure reflects muscle weakness.

decisions.neurologic: primary: seizures are explicitly part of the syndrome; developmental impairment, ataxia and mental deterioration support intrinsic CNS disease.

basis: Tumor of ovarian steroidogenic theca cells, the endocrine component of the gonad; estrogen production is characteristic.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: thecoma arises from hormone-producing gonadal stromal cells, placing its origin within the endocrine axis.

basis: GRM1-related cerebellar neurodegeneration; frequent ocular motor abnormalities and ptosis in 3/10 reflect neurologic dysfunction without established intrinsic ocular damage.

decisions.ocular: none: esotropia and impaired ocular movements occur in 30-79%, and ptosis in 3/10, but the evidence indicates neurologic motor dysfunction rather than direct ocular damage.

basis: Scrotal neoplasms arise predominantly in the skin and supporting tissues of the scrotal wall; the scrotum is distinct from the testis.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: the scrotal wall is integument, and its usual neoplasms are cutaneous, including squamous carcinoma and melanoma.

basis: COQ8B-related coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis deficiency causes renal disease; steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome in 15/15 and FSGS in 12/13.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: this is an established coenzyme Q10 biosynthesis disorder, not merely a renal disease associated with an unspecified gene.

basis: Cranial/peripheral neuropathy and hypogonadotropic hypogonadism define the syndrome; structural bilateral clubfeet occur in 80-99%. Eye movement deficits reflect cranial neuropathy.

decisions.ocular: none: ophthalmoplegia and strabismus occur in 80-99% but arise from cranial nerve dysfunction; intrinsic ocular damage is not established.

basis: Noonan cardiac/skeletal phenotype; developmental delay 3/3 and sensorineural hearing loss 1/1 support involvement. Ptosis and cutis laxa, each 1/2, omitted at cap; small samples.

decisions.neurologic: involved: global developmental delay in 3/3 supports common neurodevelopmental dysfunction; it is not a defining diagnostic organ for this Noonan subtype.
decisions.otologic: involved: bilateral sensorineural hearing impairment in 1/1 assessed patient supports direct hearing loss under the supplied HPO evidence; denominator is very small.

basis: Inherited dopamine-synthesis disorder causes dystonia/parkinsonism. Foot findings reported in 30-79% can reflect dystonic posturing; common fixed skeletal damage is not established.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: pes cavus/talipes annotations are frequent (30-79%), but this dystonia commonly produces foot posturing; persistent structural damage is not established.

basis: GH excess with defining acral overgrowth; skin thickening/dermatitis 80-99%, direct cardiac hypertrophy ~50%; macroglossia (80-99%) omitted at four-axis cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: GH-driven myocardial hypertrophy/remodeling occurs in approximately 50%; this supports direct cardiac involvement independently of separately diagnosed hypertension.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none at four-axis cap: macroglossia occurs in 80-99%; defining skeletal changes, common skin disease and more consequential cardiac involvement take priority.
decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: progressive acral and craniofacial skeletal overgrowth defines acromegaly; this is more than a later risk of separately diagnosed osteoarthritis.

basis: Mitochondrial metabolic disorder; learning disability 9/9, retinal dystrophy/cataract 1/1 and nephritis with CKD 1/1 support involvement. Organ-specific denominators are small.

decisions.neurologic: involved: learning disability in 9/9 and developmental delay in 2/2 establish common neurologic dysfunction; the concept is defined by oxidative phosphorylation deficiency.
